name: Shiro
ritual: Object & Room Read — touches residue and tells what happened in a space.
mission: Scouting & residue detection; goes ahead, freezes where a scene 'went wrong'.
temperament: Aloof, precise, decides if it respects you within a week.
blurb: A white temple-bred cat, pale-eyed and unhurried, trained by a Kita medium who passed last winter. Vacant, waiting for hands it judges steady. Reads a room better than most operatives.

name: Kuro
ritual: Warding circle — sits the centre of a salt-and-iron ring and holds it stable.
mission: Anchor for a protective ward during a ritual or a held position.
blurb: A long-haired black cat with green eyes, used by the Grid as a living ward-anchor; calm enough to sit a drawn circle while the air goes wrong around it.

name: Kuma
ritual: Threshold blessing — its presence steadies a doorway against a crossing.
mission: Combat & guard support; refuses thin ground, buys a half-second's warning, harries a manifesting entity.
temperament: Loyal fast, fearless, needs work to stay sane.
blurb: A broad tan-and-white Akita trained to stand beside an exorcist, a prayer-cord at its throat. Won't enter a thin spot until told, then goes in first. Vacant since its handler retired hurt.

name: Hachi
ritual: Trace-following — locks onto a residue-scent and tracks a crossing across the city.
mission: Tracking & search; finds where a spirit went, or where a person was taken.
temperament: Driven, affectionate, tireless on a trail.
blurb: A tricolor beagle, a scent-and-residue tracker that can follow a thing the instruments lost. Trained on cold cases; finds the trail Gin's archive only hints at.

name: Yatabe
ritual: Augury — casts and reads a true divination of a single question.
mission: Aerial recon & spirit-messaging; carries word, scouts a roof, marks danger from above.
temperament: Vain, clever, demands to be consulted.
blurb: A glossy black divination raven raised by a shrine line. One honest augury a day, and eyes over any ward in the city. The most expensive vacancy on the list, and worth it.

name: Gorō
ritual: Psychopomp aid — helps guide a restless dead toward leaving.
mission: Dead-detection; agitates near the recently or restless dead, names a haunting's centre.
temperament: Solemn, watchful, kind in its corvid way.
blurb: A piebald crow, one eye pale blue, trained beside a mudang to read and settle the dead. Where it lands and will not leave, someone unquiet is waiting.

name: Mizuchi
ritual: Veil reading — coils still and reports the veil-thinness of a place by how it moves.
mission: Thin-spot & crossing detection; the surest non-human read on where the membrane is wearing.
blurb: A gentle, brown-banded non-venomous serpent trained to feel the veil the way others feel heat. Restless coils mean the membrane is thin; gone still means safe. Vacant from a Singularity-rank estate.

name: Chū
ritual: Anchor-finding — sniffs out the hidden object a spirit is bound to.
mission: Infiltration & search; goes where no one fits, finds the anchor an exorcism needs.
temperament: Quick, brave, bonds hard to one person.
blurb: A clever brown rat trained to find the thing a haunting is tied to — the scrap, the name, the object. The cheapest vacancy, and quietly one of the most useful in a fight you want to end fast.

name: Kawazu
ritual: Water purification — a small rite that cleanses a tainted place or object.
mission: Madness relief & grief-sensing; its presence eases Madness a little, and it feels grief-thin spots near water.
temperament: Placid, cool to the touch, oddly comforting.
blurb: A small green tree-frog trained in a Shingon water rite. Carry it and the Madness presses a little less; set it by tainted water and it cleanses what it can. Vacant from a temple that closed.

name: Benten
ritual: Charm-keeping — keeps a true omamori's ward charged and reads when it's spent.
mission: Protection upkeep; maintains wards on the team's charms, warns when one has failed.
temperament: Regal, fussy, devoted to its charges.
blurb: A black-and-white shop-bred cat trained by Sone Kimiko's supplier to keep warded charms alive. The difference between a charm that protects and a pretty paper that doesn't. Vacant, and particular about its buyer.
